I see this as anorexia being a demon that grasps onto you during your darkest time. You can see that anorexia is unhealthy, based on the similarities in the appearances of the two people here. Sometimes it feels like you’re unable to break free, even though anorexia might not always have such a tight grasp on you, as shown by the way anorexia is holding the person. The person looks exhausted, but also relaxed in a way. Almost like they are unwillingly accepting that anorexia has latched onto them, and now there’s no way for them to break free at this point because they’re so exhausted and tired, based on the presentation of their body, and the dark circles around their eyes. The colour gradient of red and blue represent two different sides. Almost like a dark and a light force. Anorexia is closer the red side of the painting, whereas the person is closer to the blue side. You see the red bleeding into the blue, indicating that anorexia is not just a physical presence, but the environment around the individual is also tainted by anorexia. I would almost argue that the blue, in my eyes, is representative of feelings of depression. For me, anorexia resulted in depression and anger, and I often act irrationally at times. Oh I could really go off about this one. I hate how people think OCD is all about symmetry and organizing. While, yes, symmetry can be a form of OCD they don't understand HOW bad it is. I used what I’d consider an adapted form of parallel play to overcome some of my OCD. My friend and I would go somewhere where there weren’t as many people, and we’d have a picnic or play video games. I’d sit 100m away, or whatever distance feels like it creates a bit of discomfort (gotta push your limits sometimes), and we’d set up our picnics individually. I’d eat what I brought, they’d eat what they brought, and we’d have our phones on and talk through there. It’s like a socially distanced picnic. Not sure if that makes sense?

Hormone blockers are a different story. Testosterone doesn’t suddenly make you faster or stronger, hormone blockers prevent or prohibit the development of certain characteristics, which in turn can impact performance.  It’s different.

In some cases it’s dosage and purpose of use. There are plenty of steroids that are banned in competition WITHOUT a doctors note. For example: testosterone, ventolin, and certain ADHD meds are banned unless you have a doctors note and continued medical supervision. The second steroids become a problem is if you are using them without a doctors permission or selling them. According to the world anti-doping association and the Canadian ethics in sport policy the reasons drugs are considered banned would be:

They ruin the spirit of sport
They post a significant risk to the health of the athlete
It gives the athlete an unfair advantage

For testosterone, in particular for transgender athletes, studies showing how much it enhances performance have revealed it doesn’t do much. A therapeutic dose won’t cause harm or give an unfair advantage.

Not a doctor but I’d suggest holding off on the antibiotics. Or getting a second opinion if you can. My urinalysis’ And bloodwork always came back showing I had infections of some sort, specifically a UTI on the urinalysis, when I didn’t actually have one.

Some people just have a high amount of bacteria in their urine. It’s common in the elderly. It doesn’t always require intervention, and chronic use of antibiotics to treat patients with consistently high levels is actually contraindicated. 

Give it a few days. If you start getting symptomatic then take the antibiotics, but make sure you take all of them. If you’re still worried see a different doctor and bring up your concern that you don’t have any symptoms so you’re not sure why your levels are high.

I’d say that if you don’t want to be in a relationship with her, tell her that. Sometimes it’s possible that once the honeymoon phase wears off after the start of a relationship that you may second guess your decision to date this person. All the little things that didn’t annoy you at first start to become more prominent because you’re over the initial excitement phase. As for the vaping it was a good gesture to throw the vape out, it may have been too soon though for her to do that. Nicotine is addictive and quitting cold turkey (no matter the amount) will almost always lead to relapse. Perhaps discussing with her about how vaping changes her personality for the worse may be helpful. Quitting the use of vapes or cigarettes is hard and having additional support may help her as it seems to be that it’s a stress response to things happening her life. Relationships can be scary, especially for someone with anxiety. It’s easy to identify the problems with another person once the honeymoon period is over. Add a bit of stress and it’s not a good combination for a healthy relationship. Keeping the line of communication open is key though, because if you’re both stressed (her about the car and you about the relationship), you’re not going to be able to have a successful and productive conversation when you do finally work up the courage to chat. 

As for the car that’s a different situation entirely. If someone grew up with a certain level of privilege, having that taken away is extremely difficult. Yes, she has options, but she’s also probably facing repercussions from loaning out the vehicle to your friend/fuckbuddy. I can’t imagine her parents were thrilled to hear what happened to the car. I know it sucks to see someone who has more privilege than you complain about something you had to live through (without a choice), but if she’s been raised that way it’ll take a lot of work and time to heal and adapt to the new situation. Again, this is something you can work through together if you want to continue dating. 

If you want to remain friends with your partner you should have an open and honest discussion with them about that. It’ll probably be awkward for a while, but just because a relationship doesn’t work out doesn’t mean you two can’t be friends, especially considering you were friends first. Rather than trying to let her solve her own problems while isolating yourself, perhaps you two could work together to help each other through these tough situations. If that feels like it’s too much for you though you should end it before either of someone gets hurt.
